analysis.research_question_and_background: India has a high burden of endemic HBV and HCV infections, with national seroprevalence of 0.95% for HBV and 0.32% for HCV. In Jammu and Kashmir, the prevalence of HBV and HCV is believed to be elevated much higher than the national average.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted at a tertiary-care hospital in North Kashmir, India, from September 2023-November 2024. The study analyzed 1081 and 1087 samples for HBsAg and anti-HCV, respectively.
analysis.methods: The risk factors associated with HBV and HCV infections were analyzed statistically by using logistic regression model. The model was evaluated using AUC-ROC and F1 score. Enzyme linked immunosorbent assay(ELISA) method was used for screening Hepatitis B surface antigen and antibodies against HCV.
analysis.main_results: A total of 1081 and 1087 samples were analyzed for HBsAg and anti-HCV, which showed prevalence of 3.42% and 18.30%, respectively. Among the identified risk factors, intra venous drug usage (aOR = 18.4, P =0.000) represents the most common means of HCV transmission. Additionally, other risk factors like fever, patient type, age group of 20–40 years, and planned surgery showed statistically significant associations with HCV infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the alarming burden of HBV and HCV infection in North Kashmir compared to the national prevalence. The high prevalence of HCV infection and HBV/HCV co-infection particularly among the young population, calls for urgent, region specific screening and early diagnosis to prevent further spread of viral hepatitis infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform region-specific screening and early diagnosis strategies to prevent further spread of viral hepatitis infection. The ever-increasing incidence of both HBV and HCV infections demand region-specific screening to assess the burden of disease, risk factors and plan control measures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study. The evidence is abstract-only and provides a moderate assessment of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a cross-sectional analysis of Hepatitis B and C infections in North Kashmir, India, from September 2023 to November 2024. It found a prevalence of 3.42% for HBV and 18.30% for HCV, significantly higher than the national averages. Intra venous drug usage was identified as the most common risk factor for HCV, with other factors like fever, patient type, age group of 20–40 years, and planned surgery also showing significant associations. The study emphasizes the need for region-specific screening and early diagnosis to address the high burden of viral hepatitis in the area. The findings are based on abstract-only evidence and provide a moderate assessment of the study's conclusions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The aim of this study was to epidemiologically characterize medical emergencies and analyze the detection of hepatitis B markers in blood and blood component donors at the regional level.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Descriptive epidemiological study with data processing in Excel, 2016.
analysis.methods: The frequency, structure, and causes of emergency situations among healthcare workers, as well as information on the frequency of detection of HBsAg and/or anti-HBc totals in donors of blood and its components for 2015–2024 in the Republic of Tatarstan, were analyzed.
analysis.main_results: From 2015 to 2022, a downward trend in the incidence of chronic HBV infection was observed (9.2 and 4.1 per 100,000 population, respectively), while in 2023–2024, an upward trend was observed (7.1 and 10.8, respectively). Positive HBsAg is detected in the serum of 2–12 blood and blood component donors annually, representing 0.1–0.4 cases per 1,000 donors; anti-HBc total is detected in 64–606 donors, representing 2.3–26.2 cases per 1,000 donors. Of all registered emergency situations, 75–90 % were medical, with nursing staff accounting for the majority of casualties (57.1 %), and needlestick injuries (74.4 %) being the primary cause.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The persistent prevalence of HBV infection markers in blood and blood component donors and ongoing workplace emergencies in healthcare organizations highlight the importance of further research into the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of hepatitis B.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for continued surveillance of HBV infection trends and workplace safety measures in healthcare settings to prevent transmission and occupational exposure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to descriptive epidemiological data from a single region (Republic of Tatarstan) and may not be generalizable to other populations. The evidence strength is moderate due to the regional scope and reliance on descriptive statistics without multivariate analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a descriptive epidemiological analysis of medical emergencies and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection markers in blood donors in the Republic of Tatarstan from 2015 to 2024. Results showed a decline in chronic HBV incidence from 2015 to 2022 (9.2 to 4.1 per 100,000), followed by an increase in 2023–2024 (7.1 to 10.8). Among blood donors, HBsAg was detected in 0.1–0.4 per 1,000 donors, while anti-HBc total was found in 2.3–26.2 per 1,000. Medical emergencies accounted for 75–90% of all incidents, with needlestick injuries being the primary cause (74.4%). The findings underscore the persistent risk of HBV transmission and the need for enhanced prevention strategies in healthcare settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in HBeAg-positive and negative chronic hepatitis B patients aged over 30 years with normal ALT and detectable HBV DNA, as the 2022 update of Chinese Guidelines for Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) Management advocates initiating antiviral therapy regardless of ALT status in HBV DNA-positive patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a 96-week retrospective two-center cohort study conducted in two tertiary hospitals, involving 122 treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients aged over 30 years with normal ALT and detectable HBV DNA.
analysis.methods: The study involved standard TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) and serial assessments of virological parameters (HBV DNA quantification) and renal function markers (serum creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate) at baseline, week 48, and week 96.
analysis.main_results: After 48 weeks of TAF treatment, 74.6% of the 122 enrolled patients achieved HBV DNA conversion, and after 96 weeks, 78.7% achieved HBV DNA conversion. All patients had favorable renal tolerability throughout the treatment period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these results as demonstrating the efficacy of TAF in achieving HBV DNA conversion and its favorable renal safety profile in this specific population of patients with chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide important information for the management of chronic hepatitis B in patients aged over 30 years with normal ALT and detectable HBV DNA, supporting the use of TAF as a safe and effective treatment option.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a retrospective cohort study, which may introduce bias and limit the strength of the evidence. However, the results are based on direct observations of virological and renal outcomes in a well-defined patient population.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in HBeAg-positive and negative chronic hepatitis B patients aged over 30 years with normal ALT and detectable HBV DNA. A 96-week retrospective two-center cohort study involving 122 treatment-naïve patients found that 74.6% achieved HBV DNA conversion at 48 weeks and 78.7% at 96 weeks. All patients demonstrated favorable renal tolerability. The authors interpreted these results as evidence of TAF's effectiveness and safety in this population, which could inform treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B. The study's retrospective design may limit its evidence strength, but the findings are directly observed and relevant to clinical practice.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify host cellular factors that interact with HBV X protein (HBx) and understand their role in regulating HBx localization and viral replication. The hepatitis B virus (HBV) X protein (HBx) is a key player in viral transcription, replication, and HBV-associated hepatocarcinogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a laboratory setting using human HBV infection models. It involved the identification of host factors interacting with HBx through biochemical and cellular assays.
analysis.methods: The researchers used biochemical and cellular assays to identify HBx-interacting host factors, including colocalization studies in cytoplasmic foci or aggregates and nuclear speckles, interchromatin granule clusters (IGCs), and/or PML-nuclear bodies. They also assessed the impact of these factors on HBV replication and HBx-mediated transcription.
analysis.main_results: DDX1, DDX3, and MOV10 colocalized with HBx in cytoplasmic foci or aggregates. INI1/hSNF5 and CPSF6 relocalized with HBx in nuclear speckles, IGCs, and/or PML-nuclear bodies. Rad18 sequestered HBx in the nucleoli.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HBx-interacting host factors determine the dynamic nuclear and cytoplasmic localization of HBx and regulate HBV replication and HBx-mediated transcription. This study identified several novel factors that interact with HBx and have distinct effects on viral processes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms of HBV replication and pathogenesis, which could inform the development of targeted therapies and improve understanding of HBV-associated hepatocarcinogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence and does not provide detailed statistical analyses or experimental controls. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the lack of comprehensive data on the functional impact of these factors in vivo.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the interaction of HBV X protein (HBx) with host cellular factors and their role in regulating HBx localization and viral replication. The research identifies several novel factors, including DDX1, DDX3, MOV10, INI1/hSNF5, CPSF6, and Rad18, which interact with HBx in different subcellular compartments. DDX3, MOV10, and INI1/hSNF5 were found to restrict HBV replication, while CPSF6 facilitated it. Additionally, DDX1 enhanced HBx-mediated NF-κB transcription, whereas MOV10 and Rad18 inhibited it. The authors conclude that these HBx-interacting factors determine the dynamic localization of HBx and regulate HBV replication and transcription. The study provides important insights into the molecular mechanisms of HBV pathogenesis, which may have implications for the development of targeted therapies. However, the evidence is based solely on abstract information and lacks detailed experimental validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the current burden of hepatitis B virus infection in the United States from 2017 to 2023, addressing the need for updated epidemiological data to inform public health strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study was conducted across multiple centers in the United States, including Stanford University, Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center, and Mayo Clinic, focusing on hepatitis B virus infection data from 2017 to 2023.
analysis.methods: The analysis involved reviewing and synthesizing hepatitis B virus infection data using standardized epidemiological methods and statistical analyses to determine burden estimates.
analysis.main_results: The study provided updated estimates of hepatitis B virus infection prevalence and incidence in the United States during the specified period, though specific numerical findings were not detailed in the supplied evidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as critical for understanding the evolving landscape of hepatitis B virus infection in the U.S., highlighting the novelty of the most recent data available.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, prevention, and treatment strategies for hepatitis B virus infection, particularly in guiding public health interventions and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or the strength of the evidence, though the study's reliance on existing data may introduce potential biases or gaps in completeness.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the current burden of hepatitis B virus infection in the United States from 2017 to 2023, conducted across multiple centers including Stanford University, Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center, and Mayo Clinic. Using standardized epidemiological methods, the analysis provided updated prevalence and incidence estimates, offering critical insights for public health strategies. The findings highlight the evolving landscape of hepatitis B virus infection, informing surveillance, prevention, and treatment efforts. However, specific numerical results and limitations were not detailed in the supplied evidence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) signal-to-cutoff (S/CO) values and isolated anti-HBc positivity represent two significant diagnostic challenges in hepatitis B virus (HBV) serology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study, conducted in Karabük between 2021 and 2025, evaluated 17,356 patients screened for anti-HBc and 213 specimens with HBsAg S/CO values between 1.0 and 10.0.
analysis.methods: The study utilized HBV DNA confirmation testing and ROC analysis to determine the optimal S/CO thresholds for confirmatory testing and clarify the clinical relevance of isolated anti-HBc reactivity.
analysis.main_results: Isolated anti-HBc positivity was identified in 506 patients (2.9%), of whom 3.2% had detectable HBV DNA, with positivity significantly higher in patients older than 50 years. ROC analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.937 with an S/CO threshold of ≥3.04 achieving 100% sensitivity, while all specimens with S/CO values between 1.0 and 3.0 were HBV DNA-negative.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that HBV DNA testing may help avoid unnecessary confirmatory work-up for samples with S/CO values below 3.04 and that anti-HBc screening should be prioritized in older patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: An S/CO-based confirmatory algorithm using HBV DNA testing may improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce unnecessary clinical interventions in routine hepatitis B screening programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations, but the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to the retrospective design and reliance on abstract-only data.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study conducted in Karabük between 2021 and 2025 addressed diagnostic challenges in HBV serology by evaluating 17,356 patients screened for anti-HBc and 213 specimens with low HBsAg S/CO values. Isolated anti-HBc positivity was found in 2.9% of patients, with detectable HBV DNA in 3.2% of these cases, and positivity was significantly higher in patients over 50 years. ROC analysis established an optimal S/CO threshold of ≥3.04 with 100% sensitivity for HBV DNA detection, while all samples with S/CO values between 1.0 and 3.0 were HBV DNA-negative. The findings suggest that an S/CO-based confirmatory algorithm using HBV DNA testing can improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce unnecessary clinical interventions in routine screening.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major burden to global health, affecting more than 250 million people worldwide. While HBV-associated apolipoprotein E (apoE) and its expression in hepatocytes are known to be critical for efficient HBV infection, the importance of extracellular apoE in HBV infection has not been examined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The present study was an in vitro investigation using HepG2 cells and HepG2 NTCP cells to determine the role of extracellular apoE in HBV infection. The study utilized apoE-null HBV, cell culture supernatants from apoE3-overexpressing HepG2 cells, sera from human apoE3-knockin mice, and purified recombinant apoE expressed in E.
analysis.methods: The study employed coimmunoprecipitation experiments to assess the transfer of apoE to HBV virions. Infection assays were conducted by mixing extracellular apoE3 lipoproteins with apoE-null HBV prior to infection, and HBV attachment to cells was measured to evaluate the mechanism of action.
analysis.main_results: ApoE was efficiently transferred to HBV virions when mixed with an apoE-null HBV. Extracellular apoE3 lipoproteins significantly promoted HBV infection in a dose-dependent manner, and this enhancement was observed with apoE3-containing mouse sera, supernatants of apoE3-overexpressing HepG2 cells, and lipidated recombinant apoE3. Additionally, extracellular apoE3 lipoproteins dose-dependently enhanced HBV attachment to HepG2 NTCP cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings to demonstrate that extracellular apoE3 plays a key role in HBV infection by exchangeable transfer to the HBV envelope and mediation of HBV cell attachment. The study uncovers a previously unrecognized role of extracellular apoE3 in the promotion of HBV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that apoE3 lipoproteins with various densities in the plasma of chronic hepatitis B patients may play a key role in HBV infection and pathogenesis in vivo. This highlights the potential of extracellular apoE as a factor influencing viral entry and disease progression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study design or the strength of the evidence beyond the in vitro context. The evidence is derived from an abstract, which restricts the assessment of potential biases or confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major global health burden, and while the role of intracellular apolipoprotein E (apoE) is established, the impact of extracellular apoE was unclear. This in vitro study investigated the role of extracellular apoE in HBV infection using HepG2 cells, apoE-null HBV, and various sources of apoE3, including mouse sera and recombinant protein. Results showed that extracellular apoE3 efficiently transferred to HBV envelopes and significantly promoted HBV infection and cell attachment in a dose-dependent manner. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized function of extracellular apoE3 in enhancing HBV infectivity. The authors suggest that plasma apoE3 lipoproteins may influence HBV pathogenesis in vivo, offering new insights into viral entry mechanisms.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Preterm birth is a major adverse neonatal outcome associated with maternal hepatitis B virus carrier status, and the co-occurrence of this carrier status with gestational diabetes mellitus increases preterm birth risk compared with carrier status alone. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a clinically applicable multivariable prediction model incorporating clinical risk factors and maternal blood biomarkers to estimate preterm birth risk in women with concurrent hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was performed using clinical data and maternal blood biomarkers from 882 pregnant women with hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus who delivered at Women’s Hospital in Zhejiang Province, China, from January 2015 to December 2024. Following data preprocessing, participants were randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. A total of 847 women were included in the study, of whom 187 (22%) experienced preterm birth.
analysis.methods: Variable selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess associations of clinical variables and maternal blood biomarkers with preterm birth. Model discrimination and calibration were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and calibration plots, while clinical utility was assessed through decision curve analysis. A nomogram was developed to facilitate clinical application.
analysis.main_results: Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified pre-pregnancy body mass index, diastolic blood pressure, systolic blood pressure, alanine aminotransferase, placenta previa, white blood cell count, and maternal blood biomarkers—including total protein, total bile acid, total thyroxine, mode of membrane rupture, and prothrombin time—as independent predictors of preterm birth. The area under the curve was 0.854 (95% CI: 0.823–0.881) in the training set and 0.754 (95% CI: 0.697–0.806) in the validation set. Decision curve analysis indicated that the nomogram provided favorable clinical utility for predicting preterm birth.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating that the model has good discriminative ability and calibration, enabling accurate prediction of preterm birth risk in women with concurrent hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus. The study presents a novel nomogram incorporating specific clinical factors and blood biomarkers to address the increased risk associated with the co-occurrence of these conditions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform clinical surveillance and risk assessment by providing a tool to estimate preterm birth probability in pregnant women with both hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus. This nomogram may assist clinicians in identifying high-risk patients for targeted monitoring and potential intervention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations, potential biases, or confounding factors beyond the retrospective nature of the analysis. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to the external validation and reported performance metrics, though the reliance on data from a single center may affect generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This study addressed the increased risk of preterm birth in women with concurrent hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus by developing and validating a multivariable prediction model. Using retrospective data from 847 pregnant women in China, the researchers employed LASSO and logistic regression to identify independent predictors, including pre-pregnancy body mass index, blood pressure, liver enzymes, and specific blood biomarkers. The resulting nomogram demonstrated good calibration and discrimination, with an area under the curve of 0.854 in the training set and 0.754 in the validation set. Decision curve analysis confirmed favorable clinical utility. These findings provide a clinically applicable tool for estimating preterm birth risk in this specific population, potentially aiding in targeted surveillance and management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B remains a critical global health challenge with few patients achieving spontaneous clearance of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), a key indicator of functional cure. The study aimed to compare T cell receptor fingerprints between patients with or without HBsAg clearance after pegylated interferon alpha-2b added on nucleos(t)ide analogues.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This observational study enrolled six male patients without cirrhosis, divided equally into a group achieving HBsAg clearance and a group that did not after 48 weeks of combined therapy. Patients in both groups had comparable age, gender, baseline hepatitis B virus DNA, HBsAg, hepatitis B envelop antigen, total bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase and cirrhosis status, and all had received at least one year of nucleos(t)ide analogues before pegylated interferon alpha-2b therapy.
analysis.methods: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were isolated from participants, and 200 ng of RNA from each sample was extracted for standard RNA sequencing to construct a complementary DNA library. T cell receptor repertoire profiles were screened and compared between the two groups using RNA sequencing and bioinformation analysis.
analysis.main_results: Compared to the non-clearance group, the clearance group had significantly higher T cell receptor diversity in both alpha and beta chains, including more unique clonotypes (P = 0.017, P = 0.038 respectively) and more repertoire overlap (P = 0.002, P = 0.002 respectively). The clearance group also exhibited a broader complementarity-determining region3 length distribution and higher Chao1 index (P = 0.016, P = 0.048 respectively).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that patients with HBsAg clearance had a more diverse and robust T cell response, which may correlate with HBsAg clearance status. This finding highlights the potential role of T cell receptor diversity in functional cure.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These immune signatures may serve as potential reference indicators for pegylated interferon alpha-2b treatment response in chronic hepatitis B patients. The findings could inform strategies for monitoring or predicting functional cure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is low due to the very small sample size of six patients and the observational study design. The supplied evidence does not report on potential confounding factors or the generalisability of the findings to broader populations.

analysis.summary_en: This observational study compared T cell receptor fingerprints in six chronic hepatitis B patients who did or did not achieve hepatitis B surface antigen clearance after 48 weeks of pegylated interferon alpha-2b added to nucleos(t)ide analogues. Using RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, the study found that patients with clearance had significantly higher T cell receptor diversity, including more unique clonotypes and greater repertoire overlap, compared to those without clearance. The authors conclude that a more diverse and robust T cell response correlates with HBsAg clearance, suggesting these immune signatures could serve as potential indicators of treatment response. However, the evidence strength is low due to the small sample size and observational design.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to review the evidence available for managing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in special situations, including hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, due to the clinical challenges posed by immunosuppression and comorbidities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a narrative review based on a systematic search in PubMed and guidelines from ECCO, GETECCU, ACG, and GETAID, prioritizing publications from the last five years.
analysis.methods: The review involved a systematic search of PubMed and clinical guidelines to synthesize evidence on IBD management in special situations, with a focus on HBV screening and antiviral prophylaxis.
analysis.main_results: Universal serological screening for HBV is mandatory, and antiviral prophylaxis is required in patients who are HBsAg positive to prevent reactivation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors emphasize that managing IBD in special situations, including HBV infection, requires individualized decisions based on the best available evidence and a multidisciplinary approach.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform clinical practice by highlighting the importance of HBV screening and prophylaxis in IBD patients to prevent viral reactivation and improve outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the review is narrative and relies on existing guidelines, which may not include the most recent or high-quality studies.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses the management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in special situations, focusing on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. The study highlights that immunosuppression in IBD patients increases the risk of HBV reactivation, necessitating universal serological screening and mandatory antiviral prophylaxis for HBsAg-positive individuals. The narrative review synthesizes evidence from PubMed and clinical guidelines, emphasizing the need for individualized, multidisciplinary care. Key findings include the importance of HBV screening before initiating biologics and the safety of antiviral therapy in preventing reactivation. The evidence strength is moderate, based on existing guidelines and recent publications.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to document an observed increase in hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance during the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study included 188 patients with chronic hepatitis B aged 18 years and older who were followed between 2010 and 2023 at three hospitals in Türkiye.
analysis.methods: The study determined rates of HBsAg seroclearance, seroconversion, and serological response, analyzing data from patients who developed HBsAg seroclearance during the pandemic compared to before 2020.
analysis.main_results: A total of 26 (13.8%) patients developed HBsAg seroclearance, with 22 (84.6%) occurring in 2020 or later and 4 (15.4%) before 2020. Annual incidence rates of HBsAg seroclearance were 0.78% in 2014, 0.6% in 2017, 1.15% in 2019, 1.71% in 2020, 2.23% in 2021, 7.4% in 2022, and 1.2% in 2023.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating an increase in HBsAg seroclearance rates during the pandemic period compared to pre-pandemic years.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential impact of the COVID-19 pandemic environment or associated factors on the natural history of chronic hepatitis B, specifically regarding HBsAg seroclearance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific study design limitations, but the evidence strength is assessed as low due to the abstract-only nature of the data and the lack of detailed statistical methodology.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on HBsAg seroclearance rates in 188 chronic hepatitis B patients followed at three hospitals in Türkiye between 2010 and 2023. Results showed that 26 patients achieved seroclearance, with 84.6% of these cases occurring in 2020 or later. Annual incidence rates increased from 1.15% in 2019 to peaks of 2.23% in 2021 and 7.4% in 2022, compared to lower rates in pre-pandemic years. The authors conclude that the pandemic period was associated with an increase in HBsAg seroclearance, noting that 95% of patients were vaccinated against COVID-19 and 36.4% had a COVID-19 infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are blood-borne infections with the potential for mother-to-child transmission and remain important concerns in antenatal care in sub-Saharan Africa. This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of these infections among pregnant women in Ekiti South, Nigeria.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study recruited 710 pregnant women from six Local Government Areas in Ekiti South Senatorial District, Nigeria, to determine the seroprevalence of HBV, HCV, and HIV.
analysis.methods: Sociodemographic data and information on knowledge, awareness, and attitudes were collected using a structured questionnaire, and venous blood specimens were screened for hepatitis B surface antigen, anti-HCV antibodies, and HIV antibodies.
analysis.main_results: The overall seroprevalence was 2.5% (18/710) for HBV, 1.5% (11/710) for HIV, and 0% for HCV, with no co-infections detected. Age group was significantly associated with HIV infection (p < 0.001), whereas other sociodemographic variables were not significantly associated with HIV status or HBsAg positivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate an intermediate level of HBV endemicity in the study population, supporting the need for sustained antenatal screening and prevention of mother-to-child transmission services.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the importance of continued antenatal screening and health education to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HBV in the region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the sample may not be fully representative of all pregnant women in the region. The evidence strength is moderate due to the study design and sample size.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study determined the seroprevalence of hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) among 710 pregnant women attending antenatal care in Ekiti South, Nigeria. The overall seroprevalence was 2.5% for HBV, 1.5% for HIV, and 0% for HCV, with no co-infections detected. Age group was significantly associated with HIV infection, while other sociodemographic variables were not significantly associated with HIV status or HBsAg positivity. The findings indicate an intermediate level of HBV endemicity in the study population, supporting the need for sustained antenatal screening and prevention of mother-to-child transmission services. The study highlights the importance of continued antenatal screening and health education to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HBV in the region. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the sample may not be fully representative of all pregnant women in the region, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B remains a major global public health problem, particularly in areas of high endemicity such as Madagascar, where prevalence exceeds 8%. Rapid diagnostic tests offer a practical alternative to ELISA, but their performance in this context has yet to be evaluated.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective descriptive and analytical study compared the performance of the Virucheck® rapid test and the Wantai Bio Pharm ELISA for the detection of hepatitis B virus surface antigen. The sample consisted of 74 serum samples from patients with sickle cell disease and subjects followed at the JRA University Hospital.
analysis.methods: The study compared the Virucheck® rapid test against the Wantai Bio Pharm ELISA for detecting hepatitis B virus surface antigen. Performance metrics including sensitivity and specificity were calculated to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of both methods.
analysis.main_results: The results showed a seroprevalence of 6.75% by rapid diagnostic test versus 9.45% by ELISA. The rapid diagnostic test had a sensitivity of 71.41% and a specificity of 100%, while the ELISA confirmed its superiority with sensitivities exceeding 95% and specificities close to 98%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted a predominantly young population, reflecting the significance of mother-to-child transmission, as well as a notable seroprevalence among young adults linked to risky sexual behaviors. Optimizing hepatitis B screening in Madagascar relies on the complementary use of rapid tests for community-based screening and ELISA for diagnostic confirmation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the urgency of early and targeted screening, combined with a strengthened vaccination strategy. This approach represents a strategic pathway to reduce transmission, improve vaccination coverage, and strengthen the fight against hepatitis B in a context of high endemicity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations, bias, or confounding factors. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the data and the small sample size of 74 participants.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective study evaluated the performance of rapid diagnostic tests versus ELISA for hepatitis B screening in Madagascar, using 74 serum samples from patients with sickle cell disease and hospital subjects. ELISA demonstrated superior performance with sensitivities exceeding 95% and specificities near 98%, detecting a seroprevalence of 9.45% compared to 6.75% by the rapid test, which showed 71.41% sensitivity and 100% specificity. The findings highlight a high burden among youth, indicating mother-to-child and sexual transmission risks. The authors conclude that optimizing screening requires combining rapid tests for community use with ELISA for confirmation, alongside enhanced vaccination strategies to reduce transmission in this high-endemicity setting.

analysis.research_question_and_background: More than 5 million people in Ethiopia are living with chronic Hepatitis B virus, yet only 41.54% of individuals had good practice towards prevention, and there are research gaps on prevention practices in the country.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An institution-based mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted among 666 Medical and Health Sciences students at the University of Gondar from March to August 2025 using stratified sampling.
analysis.methods: Data were collected via a self-administered questionnaire and key informant interviews with instructors and students, analyzed using bi-variable and multivariable logistic regression and inductive thematic analysis.
analysis.main_results: 51.8% (95% CI: 48.0, 55.6) of participants had good HBV prevention practice; being 20–24 years old (AOR 2.54), a Physiotherapy student (AOR 5.41), and having a favorable attitude (AOR 2.63) were significantly associated with good practice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating low knowledge, attitude and practice regarding HBV prevention among students, with qualitative data highlighting inadequate awareness, PPE shortages, and a reliance on traditional medicine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the University and Ministry of Health should provide practical training, address PPE shortages, ensure HBV screening and vaccination, and create culturally sensitive awareness campaigns.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations or a detailed assessment of evidence strength beyond the cross-sectional nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This institution-based mixed-methods cross-sectional study assessed hepatitis B prevention practices among 666 Medical and Health Sciences students at the University of Gondar, Ethiopia, from March to August 2025. Data were collected using self-administered questionnaires and key informant interviews. The study found that 51.8% of participants had good HBV prevention practice. Multivariable analysis showed that being aged 20–24, being a Physiotherapy student, and having a favorable attitude were significantly associated with good prevention practices. Qualitative findings highlighted inadequate awareness, personal protective equipment shortages, and a reliance on traditional medicine. The authors recommend that the University and Ministry of Health provide practical training, address resource shortages, ensure vaccination, and develop culturally sensitive awareness campaigns to improve prevention practices.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Long-term use of nucleos(t)ide analogues has been associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and potential adverse effects. This study aimed to evaluate nephrotoxicity in treated and treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients and to explore DNA methyltransferase 1 expression as a potential epigenetic mechanism.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Adult chronic hepatitis B patients receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or entecavir for at least 12 months comprised the under-treatment group, while untreated patients formed the treatment-naïve group. A total of 158 patients were analyzed, including 91 treated and 67 treatment-naïve individuals.
analysis.methods: Renal parameters at baseline and months 3, 6, and 12 were analyzed retrospectively, and longitudinal changes in glomerular filtration rate were assessed using linear mixed-effects modeling. DNA methyltransferase 1 expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells was evaluated as a pilot analysis.
analysis.main_results: Median glomerular filtration rate values declined significantly from 102.3 at baseline to 102.1 at the 12th month in the treated group. Longitudinal analysis showed each additional time point was associated with a mean GFR decline of 1.65 mL/min/1.73m2, and age was independently associated with a reduction in GFR. No significant differences in renal outcomes were observed between tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and entecavir, and DNA methyltransferase 1 expression was comparable between groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating a significant decline in renal function over time in treated patients, with age identified as an independent factor. The study suggests that while nephrotoxicity is present, it does not differ significantly between the two specific nucleos(t)ide analogues studied.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings cautiously inform the monitoring of renal function in chronic hepatitis B patients undergoing long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. The results suggest that vigilance regarding kidney health is warranted regardless of the specific agent used.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the retrospective design and the abstract-only nature of the available data. The pilot epigenetic analysis was limited to a small sample size of 25 patients.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated nephrotoxicity and DNA methyltransferase 1 expression in 158 chronic hepatitis B patients, comparing those treated with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or entecavir for at least 12 months to treatment-naïve controls. Longitudinal analysis revealed a statistically significant decline in median glomerular filtration rate in the treated group over 12 months, with age identified as an independent factor for reduced renal function. No significant differences in renal outcomes were observed between the two nucleos(t)ide analogues, and the pilot epigenetic analysis found comparable DNA methyltransferase 1 expression between groups. These findings suggest the need for renal monitoring during long-term therapy, though the evidence is limited by the retrospective design and small pilot sample.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus infection remains a deadly global health issue affecting around 275 million individuals despite the availability of effective vaccines. This study investigated the adsorption behavior of the hepatitis B drug Entecavir on silica infused with gold, silver, and platinum nanocomposites to explore potential drug delivery improvements.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not report a specific study design, setting, dates, or human or animal population. The research utilized a theoretical computational approach involving density functional theory and molecular docking simulations to analyze the interaction between the drug Entecavir and metal-infused silica nanocomposites.
analysis.methods: The study employed density functional theory linked to the B3LYP functional with a combined basis set of 6-311++g(d,p) and LANL2DZ to optimize geometry and calculate adsorption energies. Natural Bond Orbital and Molecular Electrostatic Potential analyses were conducted to assess electron transfer and active sites, while molecular docking was performed to evaluate binding interactions with proteins 3OX8 and 3OXR.
analysis.main_results: Entecavir adsorbed on silver, gold, and platinum-infused silica via its NH2 group with counterpoise-corrected energies of -60.13, -39.39, and -48.33 kcal/mol, respectively. Molecular docking revealed that the drug-nanocomposite complexes effectively bind to proteins 3OX8 and 3OXR, with binding energies of -4.87, -6.11, -9.72, and -9.35 kcal/mol for Entecavir and the platinum complex, respectively, forming multiple hydrogen bonds.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the electron transfer from the nanocomposites to the drug and the favorable binding energies as confirmation of silica's role as an electron donor and the enhanced stability of the complexes. The novelty lies in the theoretical demonstration that metal-doped silica nanocomposites can create active sites for effective Entecavir adsorption and potentially improve its biological activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that silica infused with gold, silver, or platinum could serve as effective nanocarriers for the delivery of Entecavir. This theoretical insight may inform the future development of optimized drug delivery systems to enhance the treatment efficacy for chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is low because the study is entirely theoretical and computational, lacking in vitro or in vivo validation. The supplied evidence does not report experimental data, sample sizes, or physical synthesis of the nanocomposites, which limits the ability to confirm the biological relevance of the calculated interactions.

analysis.summary_en: This theoretical study investigated the adsorption of the hepatitis B drug Entecavir on silica infused with gold, silver, and platinum nanocomposites using density functional theory and molecular docking. Results showed that Entecavir adsorbed via its NH2 group with energies ranging from -60.13 to -39.39 kcal/mol and formed stable complexes with target proteins, exhibiting binding energies between -4.87 and -9.72 kcal/mol. The authors concluded that these metal-doped nanocomposites act as electron donors and enhance drug stability, suggesting their potential as effective nanocarriers for hepatitis B treatment. However, the evidence strength is low due to the absence of experimental validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health burden with persistently high morbidity and mortality, and dysregulation of the tumor microenvironment associated with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV)/hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection contributes to tumor progression and adverse outcomes. The study aimed to address the limitation that many existing HCC prognostic models do not systematically integrate infection-associated molecular signatures with immune and genomic features.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study established an integrated predictive framework based on multi-cohort transcriptomic, somatic mutation, immune infiltration, and clinical data from public databases including TCGA-LIHC, ICGC-LIRI-JP, and GEO-GSE14520. The prognostic risk model was developed in the TCGA-LIHC training cohort and externally validated in ICGC-LIRI-JP and GSE14520 cohorts.
analysis.methods: The researchers constructed a comprehensive 248-gene infection-associated set covering HBV/HCV infection, antiviral responses, and immune regulation, and identified two robust HCC molecular subtypes through unsupervised consensus clustering. They screened 12 core prognostic genes using three complementary machine learning algorithms and evaluated the model using area under the curve (AUC) values, hazard ratios, and decision curve analysis.
analysis.main_results: The study identified two HCC molecular subtypes with distinct infection-status annotations, immune infiltration features, genomic alteration profiles, and clinical prognosis. The prognostic risk model achieved 1-year AUC values of 0.82, 0.78, and 0.75 in the TCGA-LIHC, ICGC-LIRI-JP, and GSE14520 cohorts, respectively, and showed independent prognostic value for HCC with a hazard ratio of 2.87 (P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest associations among infection-associated molecular characteristics, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and HCC prognosis. The authors interpret the findings as indicating that the infection-associated signature may support retrospective HCC risk stratification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The infection-associated signature may support retrospective HCC risk stratification, offering potential improvements in predictive performance for infection-associated HCC populations compared to traditional clinicopathological models. Prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on retrospective cohorts and the need for future prospective studies.

analysis.summary_en: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major global health burden often associated with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. This study developed an integrated predictive framework using multi-cohort transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical data to address gaps in existing prognostic models. The researchers constructed a 248-gene infection-associated set, identified two distinct HCC molecular subtypes, and developed a 12-gene prognostic risk model using machine learning. The model demonstrated robust performance in training and validation cohorts, with 1-year AUC values ranging from 0.75 to 0.82 and independent prognostic value (HR = 2.87, P < 0.001). These findings suggest that infection-associated molecular characteristics are linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and HCC prognosis. While the signature shows promise for retrospective risk stratification, prospective validation is necessary before clinical application.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess five-year seroreactivity trends of hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in Northern Cyprus, with emphasis on the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and post-pandemic periods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated 278,016 serological test results from a tertiary hospital in Northern Cyprus between 2020 and 2024.
analysis.methods: Tests for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), anti-HCV, and anti-HIV were performed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay technology on the ARCHITECT Plus ci4100 system, with annual rates of seroreactivity calculated and compared across years and sex groups.
analysis.main_results: Overall seroreactivity rates were 1.2% for HBsAg, 0.6% for anti-HCV, and 0.2% for anti-HIV; HBV seroreactivity declined significantly from 1.5% in 2020 to 1.0% in 2023-2024 (p=0.001), while HCV prevalence increased non-significantly from 0.5% to 0.7% (p=0.192) and HIV prevalence remained stable at 0.2% (p=0.043).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that Northern Cyprus remains a low-endemic region, noting a declining trend in HBV seroreactivity, a rising trend in HCV levels, and stable low levels of HIV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the importance of sustained surveillance and prevention efforts for these blood-borne infections in the post-COVID-19 era.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The authors stated that results need to be interpreted cautiously as they may not entirely indicate the levels of infection, and the evidence is assessed as moderate due to the retrospective design and reliance on serological data from a single center.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated 278,016 serological test results for HBV, HCV, and HIV in Northern Cyprus between 2020 and 2024. Overall seroreactivity rates were 1.2% for HBsAg, 0.6% for anti-HCV, and 0.2% for anti-HIV. HBV seroreactivity declined significantly from 1.5% in 2020 to 1.0% in 2023-2024 (p=0.001), while HCV prevalence showed a non-significant increase from 0.5% to 0.7% and HIV prevalence remained stable at 0.2%. The authors conclude that Northern Cyprus remains a low-endemic region and emphasize the importance of sustained surveillance and prevention in the post-COVID-19 era, though they note that results should be interpreted cautiously as they may not fully reflect infection levels.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B remains a major challenge, as conventional therapies struggle to eliminate the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and subsequently restore adaptive antiviral immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed a self-assembled nanomedicine (LGN) by co-assembling lycorine with glycyrrhizic acid to overcome the limitations of lycorine and enhance its therapeutic potential against HBV.
analysis.methods: The strategy involved co-assembling lycorine with glycyrrhizic acid to create a nanomedicine that protected lycorine from premature degradation, enabled sustained release in the colon, and attenuated systemic toxicity.
analysis.main_results: LGN effectively suppressed HBsAg secretion (IC 50 = 2.15 ± 0.09 μM) with a selectivity index (SI > 93) over two-fold higher than that of lycorine alone (SI = 39.26), and concurrently inhibited HBV DNA replication, pgRNA transcription, and the expression of viral proteins HBc and HBx.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that LGN induces a distinct host transcriptional program that disrupts multiple critical stages of the HBV life cycle, including viral entry, covalently closed circular DNA maintenance, gene transcription, and immune evasion, representing a multitargeted, host-dependent mechanism distinct from nucleos(t)ide analogs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide valuable insights into exploiting natural products like lycorine for antiviral therapy and underscore the potential of self-assembly technology in improving drug safety and pharmacokinetic profiles for HBV treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study demonstrates therapeutic potential against HBV with apparent safety in the HDI model, but the evidence strength is moderate as it is based on an abstract-only report without detailed methods or long-term clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B by developing a self-assembled nanomedicine (LGN) using lycorine and glycyrrhizic acid. LGN overcomes the limitations of lycorine, such as cytotoxicity and short half-life, by enabling sustained release and reducing systemic toxicity. The nanomedicine effectively suppresses HBsAg secretion with a higher selectivity index than lycorine alone and inhibits multiple stages of the HBV life cycle, including DNA replication and viral protein expression. Transcriptomic analysis reveals LGN disrupts critical HBV lifecycle stages through a host-dependent mechanism. This approach highlights the potential of natural products and self-assembly technology for safer and more effective HBV therapy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vietnam has low hepatitis B vaccination coverage among adults, posing a threat to the healthcare system. To mitigate negative impacts, it is essential to identify vaccine hesitancy and refusal levels and their sociodemographic correlates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 926 adults in Ho Chi Minh City (January–March 2025) using a self-administered questionnaire and the Vaccination Attitudes Examination (VAX) scale.
analysis.methods: Descriptive analysis was performed, and associations between variables were explored using a chi-square test. Multinomial logistic regression identified correlates of vaccine hesitancy and refusal, statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
analysis.main_results: When analyzing general vaccine intentions regardless of vaccination status, 65.6% of participants indicated acceptance, 19.3% hesitancy, and 15.1% refusal. Vaccine refusal was primarily associated with a preference for natural immunity, while mistrust of vaccine benefits and commercial concerns were specifically linked to increased hesitancy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A unique 'knowledge paradox' was identified: poor knowledge about the HBV vaccine predicted outright refusal, whereas higher factual knowledge was positively correlated with mistrust of vaccine benefits, worries about future effects, and total VAX scores. This suggests that limited knowledge contribute to refusal, while greater factual knowledge coexisting with 'informed skepticism' or cautious hesitancy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The VAX scale serves as a reliable instrument for assessing vaccine attitudes among urban Vietnamese adults. It helps identify key vaccine-related concerns and supports continuous monitoring of public attitudes, which is essential for designing effective vaccination programs and enhancing public trust in vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or bias. The overall Cronbach's alpha was 0.833 (range = 0.812–0.919), and the McDonald's omega coefficients ranged from 0.820 to 0.920, indicating high evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated hepatitis B vaccine acceptance among urban Vietnamese adults, finding that 65.6% accepted the vaccine, 19.3% were hesitant, and 15.1% refused. A 'knowledge paradox' emerged: poor knowledge predicted refusal, while higher knowledge correlated with mistrust and hesitancy. Vaccine refusal was linked to preference for natural immunity, while hesitancy stemmed from mistrust of benefits and commercial concerns. The VAX scale proved reliable for assessing attitudes, with high internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.833). These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to address specific barriers and enhance vaccine acceptance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Drug-induced liver injury affects some people living with HIV (PWH) during antiretroviral therapy (ART). We examined associations of polygenic risk scores (PRS) with liver injury during ART.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We constructed PRS for individuals of African (AFR) and European (EUR) ancestry in 3,619 treatment-naïve participants from ART-naive studies of the Advancing Clinical Therapeutics Globally (ACTG) network.
analysis.methods: We derived PRS using summary statistics from the Veterans Affairs Million Veteran Program (MVP) and the Penn Medicine BioBank (PMBB). Liver injury was defined as incident grade 3 or greater alanine aminotransferase (ALT) within 48 weeks. Associations were evaluated by multivariable regression models.
analysis.main_results: Clinical variables associated with higher baseline ALT values included hepatitis B or C virus infection, increasing BMI and age, and male sex. In analyses of liver injury among 1,897 EUR participants (28 cases, 1869 controls) and 1722 AFR participants (21 cases, 1701 controls), HBV was associated with liver injury in both EUR and AFR participants, and HCV in EUR participants (p < 0.001 for each). PRSALT was not independently associated with incident liver injury in either EUR or AFR participants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: No association was observed between baseline PRSALT and subsequent liver injury following initiation of ART.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that genetic risk scores for ALT may not predict drug-induced liver injury in PWH starting ART, highlighting the importance of clinical factors like HBV and HCV infection in monitoring liver health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the small number of liver injury cases, particularly in the AFR group, which may reduce statistical power. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational design and limited sample size for the outcome.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether polygenic risk scores (PRS) for alanine aminotransferase (ALT) could predict drug-induced liver injury in people living with HIV (PWH) initiating antiretroviral therapy (ART). Using data from 3,619 treatment-naïve participants of African and European ancestry, the researchers derived PRS and defined liver injury as grade 3 or greater ALT within 48 weeks. Clinical variables associated with higher baseline ALT included hepatitis B or C virus infection, increasing BMI and age, and male sex. While HBV was associated with liver injury in both ancestry groups and HCV in European participants, PRSALT was not independently associated with liver injury. The findings suggest that genetic risk for ALT may not predict liver injury in PWH starting ART, emphasizing the role of clinical factors like HBV and HCV in monitoring liver health.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenge of spatially resolving comprehensive transcriptional landscapes in complex clinical tissues like formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) specimens to understand molecular pathogenesis in infectious diseases and cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research presents spRandom-seq, a spatial total RNA sequencing technology applied to FFPE tissues from mouse brain, olfactory bulb, breast cancer, Klebsiella pneumoniae-infected tissues, and hepatitis B virus (HBV)-positive hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.methods: spRandom-seq uses a random primer-based design to spatially resolve complete transcriptomes from host, bacteria, and nanoscale viruses in FFPE tissues, enabling discovery of lncRNAs, alternative splicing events, and spatial heterogeneity analysis.
analysis.main_results: In HBV-positive HCC samples, integrated analysis of host and viral RNAs revealed specific activation of complement and coagulation pathways across HBV-infected tumor areas, with an increased burden of copy number variations (CNVs).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret spRandom-seq as a practical and scalable approach for clinical pathology and infection diagnostics, leveraging its compatibility with existing platforms and minimal operational complexity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings enable detailed spatial transcriptomic analysis of HBV infection in HCC, informing understanding of viral pathogenesis and potential diagnostic applications in clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is derived solely from the abstract, limiting assessment of methodological rigor and validation; however, the technology's demonstrated applicability to multiple tissue types suggests moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces spRandom-seq, a spatial total RNA sequencing technology designed to resolve comprehensive transcriptomes from host, microbial, and viral RNAs in FFPE tissues. Applied to HBV-positive HCC samples, the method revealed spatial activation of complement and coagulation pathways in HBV-infected tumor regions with increased CNVs. The technology's compatibility with existing platforms and minimal complexity make it a practical tool for clinical pathology and infection diagnostics, offering new insights into viral pathogenesis and spatial heterogeneity in cancer and infectious diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine the expression of Hippo pathway-related proteins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and compare the data among patients with different underlying clinical background diseases, as the Hippo pathway has been implicated in HCC tumorigenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We collected 40 resected HCC formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded samples and categorized them into 4 groups according to pre-existing conditions: 17 samples of alcohol consumption (HCC-A), 6 samples with hepatitis B virus infection (HCC-B), 8 samples with hepatitis C virus infection (HCC-C), and 9 samples with metabolic diseases (HCC-M).
analysis.methods: Using immunohistochemistry, we investigated the Hippo pathway-related proteins YAP1, CADM1, and SOX9 in the collected HCC samples.
analysis.main_results: Hypertension was the most common disease (72.5%) among patients with HCC, followed by diabetes mellitus (47.5%). Significant findings of steatohepatitis (SH) were observed in the HCC-A (35.3%) and HCC-M (88.9%) groups compared with those in the HCC-B (16.7%) and HCC-C (0%) groups. A significant finding of metabolic dysfunction-associated SH (MASH) was also observed in the HCC-M group (88.9%), and liver cirrhosis was predominantly observed in the HCC-C group (100%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Hippo pathway-associated proteins could serve as potential therapeutic targets for MASH and MASH-related HCC if the Hippo pathway is inactivated, as SH was more predominant in the HCC-M group with Hippo inactivity (100%) than in the HCC-A group (50.0%), and the average tumor size was significantly larger in the Hippo-inactive group than in the Hippo-active group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the Hippo pathway could be a potential therapeutic strategy for MASH and MASH-related HCC, which may inform future treatment approaches and surveillance strategies for patients with metabolic disorders and HCC.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the small sample size (40 samples) and the retrospective nature of the data collection. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the lack of prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the expression of Hippo pathway-related proteins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and compared the data among patients with different underlying clinical background diseases. The researchers collected 40 resected HCC samples and categorized them into four groups based on pre-existing conditions: alcohol consumption (HCC-A), hepatitis B virus infection (HCC-B), hepatitis C virus infection (HCC-C), and metabolic diseases (HCC-M). Using immunohistochemistry, they analyzed the proteins YAP1, CADM1, and SOX9. The results showed that hypertension (72.5%) and diabetes mellitus (47.5%) were the most common diseases among HCC patients. Steatohepatitis (SH) was significantly more prevalent in the HCC-A (35.3%) and HCC-M (88.9%) groups compared to the HCC-B (16.7%) and HCC-C (0%) groups. Metabolic dysfunction-associated SH (MASH) was highly prevalent in the HCC-M group (88.9%), and liver cirrhosis was predominant in the HCC-C group (100%). The study concluded that Hippo pathway-associated proteins could serve as potential therapeutic targets for MASH and MASH-related HCC if the pathway is inactivated, as SH was more common in the HCC-M group with Hippo inactivity (100%) than in the HCC-A group (50.0%), and the average tumor size was significantly larger in the Hippo-inactive group. The findings suggest that targeting the Hippo pathway could be a promising therapeutic strategy for MASH and MASH-related HCC.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the poorly defined incidence, risk factors, and clinical implications of second primary cancers (SPCs) among gastric cancer (GC) survivors, aiming to quantify long-term risk and identify associated clinical factors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This multicenter cohort study analyzed 11,027 GC survivors (8,519 men and 2,508 women) who underwent curative-intent radical gastrectomy between 2007 and 2021 within the Multidisciplinary Alliance of Gastric Integrative Studies (MAGIS) cohort.
analysis.methods: Clinical factors associated with SPC occurrence were identified using LASSO-penalized Cox regression, and an exploratory risk-based stratification model was developed. Stage distribution comparisons were made between SPCs detected during asymptomatic surveillance and those diagnosed after symptom onset.
analysis.main_results: Among 11,027 GC survivors, 241 (2.19%) developed SPCs during up to 16 years of follow-up. The cumulative incidence of SPCs was 1.25% (95% CI, 1.03%-1.46%) at 5 years, 2.97% (95% CI, 2.55%-3.39%) at 10 years, and 4.15% (95% CI, 3.40%-4.91%) at 15 years post-gastrectomy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found distinct sex-specific patterns in SPC occurrence, with lung cancer predominating in males and cervical cancer in females, and demonstrated that asymptomatic surveillance detected SPCs at earlier stages than symptom-driven diagnosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the development of risk-adapted, organ- and sex-specific surveillance strategies for GC survivors to improve early detection of SPCs, though further validation in rigorous studies is required.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by its retrospective design, reliance on a single cohort, and lack of external validation for the risk stratification model, warranting cautious interpretation and future prospective studies.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter cohort study of 11,027 gastric cancer survivors treated with curative-intent gastrectomy between 2007 and 2021 quantified the long-term risk of second primary cancers (SPCs) and identified associated clinical factors. Using LASSO-penalized Cox regression, the authors found that 241 patients (2.19%) developed SPCs over up to 16 years of follow-up, with cumulative incidences of 1.25% at 5 years, 2.97% at 10 years, and 4.15% at 15 years. Risk factors included older age at surgery, chronic HBV/HCV infection, family history of cancer, and elevated preoperative systemic inflammation. The most frequent SPCs were lung (23.2%), colorectal (21.6%), and esophageal (12.9%) cancers, with marked sex-specific differences. SPCs detected during asymptomatic surveillance were more often diagnosed at stage I than those identified after symptom onset (47.4% vs 17.6%). The study derived a preliminary risk stratification model and concluded that SPCs represent a significant long-term health burden, supporting further evaluation of tailored surveillance strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the association between low-level residual viremia in chronic hepatitis B patients on nucleos(t)ide analogues and the development of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a retrospective case-control analysis comparing 104 HCC patients with 104 non-HCC controls who were both on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) and had unquantifiable serum HBV DNA by the conventional Cobas-Taqman assay at HCC diagnosis.
analysis.methods: Residual viremia was measured using a validated high-sensitivity droplet digital polymerase chain reaction assay, which had a lower limit of detection of 1.6 IU/mL. Serum samples were collected at the time of HCC diagnosis, 1 year before, and 2 years before diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: Residual viremia within 2 years before HCC diagnosis was observed in 82.7% of HCC patients and 49.0% of controls (p < 0.001). It was independently associated with HCC occurrence (OR 7.243, 95% CI 1.862-28.170, p = 0.004).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that residual viremia is a significant factor in the development of HCC and its progression, highlighting the need for more sensitive monitoring methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that high-sensitivity HBV DNA assays could improve the monitoring of patients on NUCs, potentially leading to better management of HBV-related HCC risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the use of a validated high-sensitivity assay and clear statistical associations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between residual viremia in chronic hepatitis B patients on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) and the development of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It found that residual viremia within 2 years before HCC diagnosis was significantly more common in HCC patients compared to non-HCC controls, with an independent association with HCC occurrence. The study used a high-sensitivity droplet digital PCR assay to detect HBV DNA, revealing that residual viremia was also linked to more advanced tumor staging and poorer outcomes. These results suggest that improved monitoring with sensitive assays may be crucial for managing HCC risk in NUC-treated patients. However, the study's retrospective design and potential confounding factors limit the strength of the conclusions, though the evidence remains robust due to the clear statistical associations observed.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in primary care clinics in Australia, aiming to describe the prevalence of chronic HBV and the uptake of the cascade of care among patients.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This prospective cohort study was conducted in 76 urban and regional primary care clinics across Victoria, Australia between 1/7/2020 and 30/6/2023, using anonymised socio-demographic, clinical and laboratory data from general practice electronic medical records.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that only 13% of patients with HBV had evidence of at least one HBV DNA test and one ALT test ordered, 3% were reviewed by clinic staff, 17% by a viral hepatitis specialist, and 20% were on treatment, with significant gaps in the cascade of care.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights significant gaps in the cascade of care for people with chronic HBV in primary care settings, with a low proportion of patients participating in all stages of care, though specific controversies or unresolved mechanisms are not detailed.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest a need for improved monitoring and management of HBV in primary care settings to address the gaps in the cascade of care and support Australia's goal of HBV elimination.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the cascade of care for chronic HBV in Australian primary care clinics, finding significant gaps in testing, specialist review, and treatment uptake. Among 491 patients with HBV, only 13% had evidence of both HBV DNA and ALT tests, 3% were reviewed by clinic staff, 17% by specialists, and 20% were on treatment. The results highlight the need for improved primary care management to achieve HBV elimination goals.

analysis.time: Published on 23 Jul 2026, with data from 2024.
analysis.location_and_population: Africa region, with 64 million people living with chronic hepatitis B (PLWHB).
analysis.event: Release of an operational toolkit for healthcare workers across all levels of care to prevent, diagnose, and manage hepatitis B, based on WHO 2024 guidelines.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: An estimated 240 million people globally live with chronic hepatitis B, with Africa accounting for 68% of new infections. In Africa, 6% of PLWHB had been diagnosed and 1.6% had received treatment by 2024, with hepatitis B causing an estimated 308,000 deaths in Africa that year.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The toolkit provides practical management algorithms adapted to five levels of care in Africa, from community to tertiary hospitals, and includes a companion mobile app with interactive treatment advisors. The response aims to scale up prevention, diagnosis, and treatment to reduce new infections and liver-related deaths.

analysis.brief_en: The Africa CDC has released an operational toolkit for healthcare workers across all levels of care to address hepatitis B in Africa, where the disease burden is disproportionately high. With 64 million people living with chronic hepatitis B in Africa, only 6% had been diagnosed and 1.6% had received treatment by 2024, despite the availability of effective diagnostics and therapy. The toolkit, based on WHO 2024 guidelines, provides practical management algorithms for community, primary care, and hospital settings, accompanied by a mobile app with interactive treatment tools. This initiative aims to improve diagnosis, linkage to care, and treatment uptake to prevent new infections and reduce the estimated 308,000 hepatitis B-related deaths in Africa annually.
